blind_target.authors: Pedroni, A., Frey, R., Bruhin, A., Dutilh, G., Hertwig, R., & Rieskamp, J.
blind_target.title: The risk elicitation puzzle.
blind_target.evidence_quote: Previous research showed evidence that risk preferences elicited with different measures may significantly differ and that the measures provide results that are not robust across the contexts (Crosetto & Filippin, 2016; Csermely & Rabas, 2016; Pedroni et al., 2017). In line with these findings, we explored the issue of risk measures consistency in our study. We found that the three risk elicitation methods did not correlate or correlated weakly.
blind_target.outcome_quote: Previous research showed evidence that risk preferences elicited with different measures may significantly differ and that the measures provide results that are not robust across the contexts (Crosetto & Filippin, 2016; Csermely & Rabas, 2016; Pedroni et al., 2017). blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The authors directly compare the tested finding with this cited original.

luna_triage.reason: The Discussion attributes cross-method risk-measure inconsistency to earlier research including Pedroni et al., then reports testing consistency across three elicitation methods and finding weak or absent correlations. This directly retests that empirical claim. The supplied shipped row 2431 is Carr and Steele (2010), a different finding. No prior adjudication exists.
